comparator.name: Bachelor Theologie en Religiewetenschappen
comparator.route: Religie en Levensbeschouwing (Zingeving, geestelijke verzorging en samenleving) track
comparator.academicYear: Fall 2026 entry, deeltijd (part-time) pace; the deeltijd variant carries the identical 180-EC curriculum and content as the voltijd programme, per s0 and s4, spread over more calendar years rather than a distinct credit structure
comparator.sourceNotes: The normalized target (cp-000119, registry row 127, canonical_name 'B Theology and Religious Studies (deeltijd, Nederlands)', source_provider_id 111A136, programme_unit_code 1001O5760, recognized_programme_code 50910, languages_json=["NLD"], modes_json=["DEELTIJD"]) names no specific route. VU's current official overview page (s0, checked 2026-09-27) confirms a 180-EC, three-year bachelor offered '3 jaar Voltijd en deeltijd' with three co-equal afstudeerrichtingen chosen from year 1: Christelijke theologie (Theologie), Islamitische theologie (Islam, which s0 itself describes as 'the only Islamic-theological WO bachelor in the Netherlands'), and Religie en Levensbeschouwing (also branded 'Zingeving, geestelijke verzorging en samenleving'); s4, a third-party study-choice aggregator republishing VU's own submitted programme data, independently confirms the 180-ECTS total and the same three afstudeerrichtingen. Applying the Section 2.1 neutral route-selection hierarchy (the target is generic and no route is clearly more representative): the Theologie track's own current page (s2) requires a compulsory Hebrew (Hebreeuws I-III) and Greek (Greek I-III + New Testament) biblical-language sequence and offers tradition-specific confessional seminary sub-tracks (Hersteld Hervormd, Baptist, Mennonite); the Islam track requires compulsory Arabic-language study and Qur'an/hadith/fiqh confessional training (s0; independently corroborated by generator-eligible programme-interest rows 5410, 5411, 5412, 5413 naming Qur'an/hadith exegesis, Sharia jurisprudence and Arabic-language study as structural Islam-track content). Religie en Levensbeschouwing is instead described by its own current page (s1) as an explicitly comparative, multireligious, 'dialogisch' course of study engaging several religious traditions rather than forming students within one confessional tradition, with no compulsory classical/liturgical-language sequence. It is therefore the least specialized/most general of the three formal routes and is selected as the reconstructed route. However, s0, s1 and s2 give only qualitative year-by-year course-name lists for their respective tracks (for the selected route: year 1 covers the origin of religious traditions and world religions plus 'Conflict and Peacebuilding'; year 2 covers 'Zingeving, religie en mentale gezondheid' and 'Religie en trauma'; year 3 includes a flexible-location minor, 'Scriptieseminar en bachelorscriptie', and electives such as 'Godsdienstfilosofie') without any EC weight, compulsory-versus-elective status, or credit table for a single component. VU's own current regulations page (s3, checked 2026-09-27) states that the formal Teaching and Examination Regulations for every VU programme are 'published in the Study Guide' at studiegids.vu.nl; that portal's landing page carries only top-level dynamic category navigation with no extractable curriculum content, and a constructed direct URL for this exact study guide entry returned HTTP 404 to available retrieval tools, matching the same dynamic-portal limitation already documented for another current VU counselor target (cp-000118). Reasonable further search located only one standalone official OER PDF for a VU theology bachelor, 'Onderwijs- en Examenregeling Bacheloropleiding Theologie 2017-2018' (s5); its own text shows 'Minor Islam' offered only as one elective minor within a single undifferentiated Theologie bachelor, not as one of three co-equal afstudeerrichtingen chosen from year 1, so it predates and does not reliably describe the current three-route structure and is preserved only as evidence of how substantially the formal structure has since changed, not used to supply component credits. No third-party source (s4; the Qompas study-choice listing checked during research) publishes a per-course EC table either. Because no accessible current or formally adopted source establishes exact EC weights, compulsory/elective status or a stable component list for the selected route, no 180-EC component list is supplied.

routeSelection.route: Religie en Levensbeschouwing (Zingeving, geestelijke verzorging en samenleving) track
routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names no specific route. Among the programme's three current co-equal afstudeerrichtingen (s0, s1, s2), Theologie requires a compulsory Hebrew-and-Greek biblical-language sequence and offers tradition-specific confessional seminary sub-tracks, and Islam requires compulsory Arabic-language study and Qur'an/hadith/fiqh confessional training; Religie en Levensbeschouwing is VU's own current page description as an explicitly comparative, multireligious, dialogical course of study with no compulsory classical/liturgical-language sequence or single-tradition confessional formation. Since no route is clearly more representative of the generic normalized target, Religie en Levensbeschouwing is the least specialized/most general of the three under the Section 2.1 tie-break rule and is selected, notwithstanding that course-level reconstruction cannot proceed until the credit structure is resolved.

exception.reason: The exact EC weights and compulsory-versus-elective status of every curriculum component in the selected Religie en Levensbeschouwing route cannot be verified from any source accessible to available tools. VU's own current regulations page states the formal OER/TER is published only inside the dynamic studiegids.vu.nl study-guide application, which returned no extractable curriculum content to available retrieval tools, and the only standalone official OER document discoverable through reasonable search (2017-2018) predates the current three-route structure -- it still treats Islam as an elective minor rather than a parallel afstudeerrichting -- and does not reliably describe the current curriculum. A complete 180-EC comparator would require inventing credit weights and compulsory/elective status that no current or formally adopted source supports, so a canonical comparison cannot be made yet.
exception.curriculumContext: VU's current official pages (checked 2026-09-27) confirm a 180-EC, three-year Bachelor Theologie en Religiewetenschappen offered voltijd and deeltijd, with three co-equal afstudeerrichtingen selected from year 1 (Theologie, Islam, and the selected Religie en Levensbeschouwing/Zingeving route); the deeltijd variant carries the identical 180-EC curriculum at a reduced pace rather than a distinct credit structure. The selected route's own page names its year-by-year course themes -- the origin of religious traditions, world religions and conflict/peacebuilding in year 1; meaning-making/mental health and religion and trauma in year 2; a flexible-location minor plus a scriptieseminar-and-bachelorscriptie and electives such as philosophy of religion in year 3 -- but supplies no EC, compulsory-status or credit-table information for any of them. Resolve the applicable current OER/study-guide credit structure for this exact merged three-route programme, or obtain a current standalone OER document that supersedes the 2017-2018 minor-based structure, before revisiting this comparator.
